p_bfda57d3f1.sentence: Only those sleeping children keep me from killing you now.
p_bfda57d3f1.prev: I told you I would kill you if you ever said one word about it!
p_bfda57d3f1.next: Take very good care of them.

p_9719c7f3d4.sentence: She melted into white mist, rose towards the roof beams, and slipped away through the smoke-hole.
p_9719c7f3d4.prev: Her voice grew thin, like the crying of the wind.

p_fd6ee8f2fb.sentence: One winter night in Japan, two woodcutters struggled through a snowstorm.
p_fd6ee8f2fb.next: Minokichi was eighteen; the old man was his master.

p_49aa03b51b.sentence: A woman dressed in white was bending over his master.
p_49aa03b51b.next: In the pale light, her breath flowed across the old man’s face like white smoke.

p_d5951614d5.sentence: I meant to kill you too,” she whispered.
p_d5951614d5.prev: Her beautiful face came close to his.
p_d5951614d5.next: But you are young, so you may live.

p_1aecdbc2fd.sentence: She stepped out into the storm.
p_1aecdbc2fd.next: Minokichi barred the door and touched his master’s face.

p_3633fe1273.prev: Minokichi barred the door and touched his master’s face.

p_d0576e65b1.sentence: He kept silent even about his master’s death.
p_d0576e65b1.prev: After that night, Minokichi told nobody what had happened.
p_d0576e65b1.next: The next winter, on the road home, he met a beautiful girl called Yuki.

p_2dcab5d82c.sentence: In time they had ten fair-skinned children.
p_2dcab5d82c.next: The children grew, but Yuki seemed never to grow old.

p_822920142f.sentence: When they could go no farther, they took shelter in a hut beside a river.
p_822920142f.prev: Minokichi was eighteen; the old man was his master.
p_822920142f.next: They barred the door and lay under their straw coats.

p_23de62b690.sentence: He took her home to his widowed mother, who welcomed the girl and persuaded her to stay.
p_23de62b690.prev: Her skin was white, and her voice was gentle.
